description:
Realistic Tariffs and Weapons Salesman

About
Annoyed for paying tariffs to a starving planet? or in need of critical goods, this mod is for you!

A small gameplay and economy mod which is vanilla friendly it replaces static global tariffs with
a more reactive & realistic system meant to add to the immersion of the game economy.
Local governments now actively lower trade barriers and provide rebates for commodity exports.

Additionally, Ship & Weapons buy & sell prices now increase if there are deficits in the Ship Hulls & Weapons commodity.
To add some extra flavor selling faction design ships to their factions provides reputation and boost
in credits when these factions are at war, like selling XIV battlegroup ships to the hegemony.

Why did I make this mod ?
First as of 2026 in vanilla Starsector you don't get a notification when there is significant demand for commodities,
secondly tariffs are not immersive or logical the main purpose of tariffs is to control imports & is usually done in a per commodity basis.
Since it's impossible or extremely complex to apply a tariff per commodity, I did the second-best thing it came to mind...
when markets cant meet the demand of multiple commodities and have these in deficit these progressively lower the tariffs on that market,
as a normal government would do.

Download

https://github.com/MightyDuck75/RealisticTariffs/releases/download/v0.9.2/RealisticTariffs.zip

https://www.nexusmods.com/starsector/mods/151?tab=files&file_id=1129

F.A.Q

1 - Does this work with Nexerelin ?

Yes, from my limited testing it works as intended due to telling in mod_info.json to run after nexerelin, nexerelin also modifies tariffs but as this mod runs after it nullfies nexerelin mod changes.

2 - Can I disable Tariff Rebates and Factional ship buybacks?

Yes, just go to the mod folder -> data -> config -> rt_settings.json and set the "isExportRebateActive" to false and the same for "isFactionBuybackProgramActive" ..

3 - Can I change tariffs values and other settings in this mod?

Yes, there is a number of settings you can change just go to mod folder -> data -> config -> rt_settings.json

4 - Do I need lw_lazylib or MagicLib to use this mod?
No, you dont need it !

5 - How do I know my current mods will work with this mod?
If your mods don't alter commodities, tariffs and ship prices it should be fine, but the best way is to start a new game see if new intel notifications are created about market deficits, buy and sell a faction design ship to confirm you get a reputation boost once, buy some commodities see if you get a rebate and if a market with at least a commodity deficit has less than 18% tariffs.

6 - Does this work with previous version of Starsector?
It shouldn't but I haven't tested..

Features

Dynamic Tariff Scaling
The mod monitors every market(planet, station..) known to the player, when a market has deficit in a commodity, the local authorities will slash tariffs to attract independent traders. The table bellow shows the impact that each commodity has on the market tariffs when on deficit, they subtract from the default of 18% until they reach the minimum value of 3%.

Why did I set these values ?
I basically wanted an important intel notification to pop up whenever there were about 2 to 3 deficits in commodities. The rest should feel immersive like, a planet running out of food or essential goods would create real political pressures, unlike just having a deficit in Marines or something. I haven't really tested these values extensively or consider numerous combinations...

Global Tariffs Range:

Min Tariffs Max Tariffs (Default)
3% 18%

Ships and weapons prices boost
Currently, in-game you have an economic demand for ship hulls and weapons, this can get into deficit as any normal commodity but doesn't affect ship or weapons prices in any way.
As I was addressing the tariff values and intel, I also decided to boost ship and weapon prices based on market demand and any ongoing factional wars (excluding terrorists and pirates). Selling ships and weapons doesn't reduce the deficit, though.

I haven't tested these values enough to determine whether the price boost gives the player too many credits. However, since selling a ship in-game often doesn't provide a big economic incentive, the impact still shouldn't be too significant and the values can always be adjusted by the player in rt_settings.json.

Key Features

The Exporter's Rebate:

Exporting goods are sales that bring new money to an economy, so it doesn't generally make sense to have export tariffs.
This mod tracks the exact amount of tariffs paid during trades and returns it to the player, effectively disabling their gameplay impact.
Upon leaving the trade menu, the government issues a full credit refund directly to the player.
Note: Rebates do not apply to illegal goods (Drugs/Organs).

Ship Market Overhaul:

Ship Hulls & Weapons Deficit Impacts Prices: Ship and weapon buying/selling prices now fluctuate based on the local market deficit.
Faction Wars Impact Prices: If a faction is at war with 1 faction, ship and weapon prices increase by +15%. If at war with 2 or more factions, prices increase by +30%.
Ship Buyback Program: If a faction is at war and has its own ship designs, selling those ships in their markets grants +10% credits and +1 reputation.
Selling XIV battlegroup ships to the Hegemony grants +20% value and +4 reputation. Selling elsewhere gives no bonus and instead causes -1 reputation (or -8 for XIV ships).

New Intel Notifications:

Custom Intel entries appear for markets with shortages. Minor shortages appear in the trade section, while major shortages appear in the important section.
Additional Intel entries highlight ship buyback programs and markets with increased ship/weapon prices due to faction wars.

Final Thoughts

This is my first mod I did to test LLMs and give me an intro into the modding in this game, took me way more time than expected,
the game didn't first supported what I wanted to do initially and I had to adapt, some feature creep and some AI hallucinations eventually
resulted on this.
I’m pretty picky with mods. I usually stick to the developer’s original vision, since mods can easily mess with the overall feel of the game.
Anything that breaks immersion is a dealbreaker for me. That said, I’m really happy with this one. It fits naturally into my vanilla
experience and improves it without getting in the way.
The exporter rebate is a workaround, but a necessary one. It might seem odd at first, but compared to how extreme the vanilla
export tariffs are, it actually feels like justice xD

If you have feedback or tips on improving modding in starsector it will be much appreciated, and will consider changes that make sense.
I’ve also got a few more mod ideas in mind to improve some bad gameplay designs, hope you find this mod useful!
